title: Observability starts with a service map
points: Map request paths, dependencies and owners before choosing telemetry.
Metrics show trends, logs explain events, traces connect requests across services.
Define user outcomes and failure boundaries before selecting alarms.

title: Metrics, logs and traces answer different questions
points: Metrics summarize numeric behavior and support alarms.
Logs retain event details with retention and access controls.
Traces reveal latency and error propagation across service hops.

title: CloudWatch metrics need the right dimensions
points: Namespace, metric name and dimension set identify a time series.
Use standard or high-resolution custom metrics where appropriate.
Avoid unbounded high-cardinality dimensions and choose useful statistics.

title: EC2 telemetry needs an agent for memory
points: Default EC2 metrics include CPU and network, not guest memory or disk used percentage.
CloudWatch agent collects OS metrics and logs with instance role permissions.
Systems Manager can distribute configuration from Parameter Store.

title: Alarms evaluate data over time
points: Period, evaluation periods and datapoints to alarm govern sensitivity.
Choose how to treat missing data and understand insufficient data state.
Composite alarms reduce alert noise while actions route to SNS or automation.

title: Alarm actions are not all the same
points: CloudWatch alarm state changes can notify SNS and emit events to EventBridge.
EC2 actions and Auto Scaling actions have specific targets and prerequisites.
Route operational response through guarded automation instead of blind remediation.

title: Logs have groups, streams and retention
points: Choose log-group boundaries by application and access policy.
Streams organize producers; set retention and KMS access deliberately.
Mask sensitive fields and avoid treating logs as unrestricted long-term storage.

title: Find errors with metric filters and Logs Insights
points: Metric filters turn matching events into count metrics for alarms.
Logs Insights queries investigate patterns and can feed dashboards.
An absent log may be an ingestion, permission, retention or query-scope problem.

title: Export and subscription have different latency
points: S3 export tasks are for bounded historical log transfer, not live alerts.
Subscription filters stream matching events to Lambda, Kinesis or Firehose.
Check destination permissions, delivery failures and recursion protection.

title: Centralize logs across accounts and Regions
points: Separate source log groups, regional destination and central analysis account.
Cross-account subscription destination policy and source filter permissions must align.
Use current centralization capability where it fits; preserve source account and Region fields.

title: Container observability follows task and node
points: ECS and EKS logs, metrics and traces have different collection paths.
Collect task/pod identity, service health and infrastructure saturation.
Distinguish deployment errors from runtime capacity and dependency failures.

title: ADOT transports OpenTelemetry signals
points: Instrument services with OpenTelemetry and route through an ADOT collector.
Control sampling, attributes and export destinations for metrics and traces.
Propagation across boundaries is essential to join a distributed request.

title: Trace a slow API request end to end
points: Correlate API Gateway, Lambda, downstream service and database spans.
Compare total latency with each segment and inspect error annotations.
Sampling and missing context can hide a hop; validate instrumentation first.

title: X-Ray service maps reveal dependency failures
points: Trace segments and subsegments show call paths and latency distribution.
Use annotations for indexed filtering and metadata for non-indexed detail.
Service maps aid diagnosis but require permissions and instrumentation.

title: Synthetics tests a journey before users do
points: A canary exercises API or browser actions on a schedule.
Capture availability, latency, screenshots and failure artifacts.
Alarm on failed journeys and distinguish canary health from real-user experience.

title: RUM observes actual browser sessions
points: CloudWatch RUM measures real user performance and errors across devices and locations.
Sampling, privacy and client configuration shape the evidence.
Compare RUM with Synthetics to separate lab failures from customer impact.

title: Application Signals connects service health to SLOs
points: Discover service operations and dependencies with Application Signals.
Use latency and availability indicators to measure user-facing performance.
Define objectives and burn-rate responses rather than paging on every spike.

title: SLI, SLO and error budget make reliability measurable
points: An SLI measures a defined good-event ratio or latency threshold.
An SLO sets target and interval; error budget is allowed failure within it.
Budget burn alerts guide release and remediation decisions.

title: Build an SLO from an API path
points: Define successful requests and exclude only justified traffic.
Set a 99.9 percent availability target over 30 days and calculate budget.
Use both fast and slow burn signals with owner and response policy.

title: AI workload telemetry includes quality and safety
points: Monitor invocation failures, latency, tokens and cost for model calls.
Track groundedness, safety and human feedback where evaluated.
Segment by model/version and use privacy-safe prompts and output handling.

title: Agent traces follow tool and approval boundaries
points: Capture agent steps, tool calls, identity and outcome without leaking secrets.
Mark human approval and guardrail decisions as distinct events.
Correlate cost and latency per user task, not just per model call.

title: Route alerts by ownership and severity
points: CloudWatch alarms and EventBridge events feed SNS, incident tools or runbooks.
Page for actionable user impact; use tickets for lower urgency drift.
Deduplicate correlated symptoms and preserve context for responders.

title: AWS Health events need resource context
points: Health events may identify account-specific affected resources and planned maintenance.
EventBridge can route relevant events to response workflows.
Public service-health information and account-specific Health events have different scope.

title: Systems Manager manages hybrid fleets
points: Managed nodes need SSM Agent, instance identity, network endpoints and permissions.
Use Inventory, State Manager and Fleet Manager for visibility and configuration.
A missing managed node is a connectivity, agent or authorization diagnostic.

title: Session Manager replaces open SSH paths
points: IAM authorizes StartSession; agent and endpoints connect managed nodes.
Session logs and CloudTrail events have distinct recording roles.
No inbound SSH or bastion is required for supported sessions.

title: Run Command requires bounded blast radius
points: Target nodes by tags or resource group and choose a reviewed document.
Set maximum concurrency and maximum errors before fleet execution.
Record command output and failed node remediation without opening SSH.

title: Automation runbooks guard state changes
points: Steps, roles and parameter validation define a repeatable remediation.
Approval, rate control and rollback/stop conditions constrain execution.
Test in a narrow scope before organization-wide use.

title: Patch Manager follows baseline and window
points: Define patch baseline and tagged targets, then schedule maintenance windows.
Run AWS-RunPatchBaseline with concurrency and error controls.
Review compliance and exceptions; patch execution is not proof of application health.

title: State Manager keeps agent configuration consistent
points: Association applies a desired configuration on schedule or change.
Store CloudWatch agent configuration in Parameter Store.
Monitor association compliance and investigate drift or failed prerequisites.

title: OpsCenter ties signals to an OpsItem
points: Aggregate alarm, Config, CloudTrail and resource context into an OpsItem.
Assign owner and severity, inspect related resources and history.
Run a vetted Automation playbook and record outcome.

title: Service quotas belong in capacity planning
points: Monitor usage against adjustable and fixed quotas for each account/Region.
Request increases before planned scale and test failover Region capacity.
A quota breach can masquerade as deployment or autoscaling failure.

title: Cloud Map resolves changing service endpoints
points: Register instances with attributes and health; clients discover by DNS or API.
Service discovery is distinct from traffic policy and load balancing.
Stale or unhealthy registrations can redirect requests incorrectly.

title: Retries need backoff, jitter and idempotency
points: Retry transient failures with bounded exponential backoff and jitter.
Use idempotency keys to avoid duplicated side effects.
Deadlines and retry budgets prevent load amplification during outages.

title: Circuit breakers and bulkheads contain failure
points: Circuit breakers stop repeated calls to an unhealthy dependency and probe recovery.
Bulkheads isolate pools so one dependency cannot exhaust all capacity.
Fallbacks must have clear freshness and correctness limits.

title: Scale on demand signals, not CPU alone
points: Choose target tracking, step or scheduled scaling for workload shape.
Queue backlog per worker and request rate may be better signals than CPU.
Cooldown, warmup, capacity bounds and quota headroom govern response.

title: Self-healing needs a safe replacement path
points: Health checks detect failure at instance, target or service level.
Auto Scaling or orchestrators replace unhealthy capacity after thresholds.
Protect state and verify replacement readiness before routing traffic.

title: Walkthrough: missing CloudWatch logs
points: Start with the application event and expected log group/stream.
Check agent/runtime logging, IAM permission, Region and subscription path.
Restore ingestion, issue a test event and verify query visibility.

title: Walkthrough: cross-account log delivery failure
points: Inspect subscription filter, destination policy, role and regional alignment.
Follow delivery errors through destination stream or Firehose.
Repair scoped permission and verify one redacted test event end to end.

title: Walkthrough: alert storm after deploy
points: Correlate deployment time with latency, 5xx, queue depth and dependency traces.
Use composite or burn-rate alerts to identify user impact.
Pause rollout, roll back safely and verify customer outcomes.

title: Walkthrough: patch a fleet without outage
points: Use a tagged canary group, maintenance window and patch baseline.
Bound concurrency and errors, verify service health between waves.
Record compliance, failed nodes and rollback or replacement decisions.

title: Walkthrough: recover a failed worker tier
points: Alarm on backlog age and failed job rate, inspect traces and capacity.
Replace unhealthy workers and preserve idempotent retry behavior.
Confirm backlog drain and user-facing SLO recovery.

title: Choose the signal and runbook for the symptom
points: Map high latency, missing logs, failing canary and unhealthy fleet to first evidence.
Pick the smallest safe intervention and an explicit rollback criterion.
Close with service health and SLO verification, not action success alone.
